title: What If We Launched Our Nuclear Waste Into the Sun?

scenes.text: What if we launched nuclear waste into the Sun? It's harder than leaving the solar system.
Earth races around the Sun at about 30 kilometers per second. Anything we launch keeps that sideways speed.
To fall into the Sun, a rocket has to cancel almost all of it.
Escaping the solar system entirely takes only about 12 kilometers per second more.
Even a cheap launch costs around 100 million dollars, and one estimate says it would take 34,000 rockets.
A failure rate of just 0.1 percent would still rain about 34 rockets' worth of waste back on Earth.
